items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: I told him that I had tried to play a little violin when I was younger.

ctx.x: He didn't know that you had thrown them away. (LAUGHTER).

We had thrown them away. I told him that I had tried to play a little violin when I was younger. But he was very nice you know. He says, it's jazz huh? Jazz. Not bad. (LAUGHTER). He says at least you can dance to it. That's about all he said. That was the finish of. it..

However, we did go back to Chicago outside of the drummer and the clarinet player, Jimmy Hartwell and Vic Moore. And Dick Voynow, we got, what did we get, I've forgotten, Oh Jimmy Lord, Jimmy Lord that's right. Lloyd on clarinet and oh, Frank, oh what was his name, on drums. And we worked a couple of jobs at the Rendezvous on the North Side and the Valentino Inn downtown and the band broke up, at that time.
